key_insight: Andromeda 2 shows that an evidence-grounded agent can iteratively design better drug formulations by combining prior experimental results with computational and lab tools. In a matched-budget autonomous lab setting, it benchmarks against an earlier system to improve the efficiency of formulation discovery.
problem_solved: Finding high-performing self-emulsifying drug delivery system (SEDDS) formulations is slow and experimentally expensive because many candidate mixtures must be tested to improve oral bioavailability for poorly soluble drugs.
method: Reasoning over structured in-house experimental evidence to guide next-step formulation choices.
Invoking computational and experimental tools to design, test, and refine successive formulation batches.
Running in a miniaturized autonomous laboratory under a matched budget and benchmarking performance against Andromeda 1.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this paper demonstrates a practical agentic workflow where evidence retrieval, tool use, and experimental feedback are tightly coupled. It suggests a path toward more data-efficient, autonomous scientific discovery systems that can outperform simpler baselines in real laboratory settings.
visual_elements: A workflow diagram showing evidence -> agent reasoning -> tool calls -> experiment -> updated evidence.

A feedback loop graphic highlighting iterative batch optimization over successive rounds.
paper_title: Evidence-Grounded Agentic Formulation Development in an Autonomous Laboratory
paper_authors: Michael M. Craig, Riley J. Hickman, Yingshan Ma, Rémi Piché-Taillefer, Christine Allen
